newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Heinz denies planning Czech unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Heinz denies planning Czech unit sale.

text.p: The Czech baby food unit of U.S. based H.J. Heinz Corp, Heinz-PMV a.s., said on Tuesday the parent company was re-considering its Czech dairy operations as part of a corporate restructuring announced last week.

A spokesman for the Heinz Czech unit in Prague said in a statement that contrary to published reports, Heinz was not planning to sell the entire PMV operation, but rather the production of dairy products at the factory was under review as part of Heinz's restructuring effort.
The statement said the part of the operation under review comprised 15 percent of total turnover of the Czech plant.
In 1995, Heinz acquired an 80 percent stake in the Czech factory, the largest maker of Czech baby formula, in the town of Zabreh.
It said the H.J. Heinz stake in the Zabreh factory is part of a region-wide strategy to supply infant formula and related products in an area vital to the realisation of Heinz long term growth plans.

The Pittsburgh-based food group Heinz said last Friday it would close or sell at least 25 plants, cut 2,500 jobs worldwide and take a 650 million pre-tax charge to cover the costs of a massive corporate reorganisation.
It said that "a Czech dairy" would be among assets that might be sold.

"The company has invested significantly in the dry products -- infant formula and related products -- section of the business which makes up over 80 percent of turnover, and will continue to do so in pursuit of its regional strategic goals," the statement said on Tuesday.
